question: Which of these is the title of the first novel of Anand Neelakantan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asura: Tale of the Vanquished.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anand Neelakantan is an Indian author, columnist and screenwriter, best known for retelling Indian epics from the point of view of the losers or the vanquished.

• His first novel was "Asura: Tale of the Vanquished" (published in 2012), which narrates the Ramayana from Ravana's perspective, along with the voice of a common Asura named Bhadra.

• He also wrote the Ajaya series (Roll of the Dice, Rise of Kali), which retells the Mahabharata from Duryodhana's (Kaurava) point of view, and "Vanara".

• He wrote the story and dialogues for popular television shows and the prequel novels of the film Baahubali (e.g., The Rise of Sivagami).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Satya Ke Prayog" (The Story of My Experiments with Truth) is the autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi, written in Gujarati and published in the 1920s.

• "The Immortals of Meluha" (2010) is the first book of the Shiva Trilogy by Amish Tripathi, followed by The Secret of the Nagas and The Oath of the Vayuputras.

• "Kadambari" is a Sanskrit romantic novel by Banabhatta, court poet of Emperor Harshavardhana; Banabhatta also wrote Harshacharita.

NOTE

• Author–book pairs are a repeated SSC theme. Remember: Amish Tripathi – Shiva Trilogy, Ram Chandra Series; Chetan Bhagat – Five Point Someone; Arundhati Roy – The God of Small Things (Booker Prize 1997); Kiran Desai – The Inheritance of Loss (Booker Prize 2006).

question: Article ______ of the Indian Constitution deals with "Right to Constitutional Remedies".
solution_text:
The correct answer is 32 – 35.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Right to Constitutional Remedies is guaranteed by Articles 32 to 35 of the Indian Constitution, in Part III (Fundamental Rights).

• Article 32 is the heart of this right — it gives a citizen the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

◦ Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the "heart and soul of the Constitution".

◦ Under Article 32 the Supreme Court can issue five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

◦ Article 226 gives the High Courts a wider writ power — for Fundamental Rights and for any other legal right.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The six Fundamental Rights and their Articles:

◦ Right to Equality – Articles 14–18

◦ Right to Freedom – Articles 19–22

◦ Right against Exploitation – Articles 23–24

◦ Right to Freedom of Religion – Articles 25–28

◦ Cultural and Educational Rights – Articles 29–30

◦ Right to Constitutional Remedies – Articles 32–35

NOTE

• The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978, and is now a legal right under Article 300A.

• Fundamental Rights were inspired by the Constitution of the USA (Bill of Rights).

question: As per the Census 2011, what is the sex ratio in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 943 females per thousand males.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the sex ratio of India was 943 females per 1000 males, an improvement over 933 recorded in Census 2001.

• Sex ratio in India is defined as the number of females per 1000 males.

• Other key Census 2011 figures:

◦ Total population – about 121.09 crore (1210.85 million).

◦ Literacy rate – 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

◦ Population density – 382 persons per sq km.

◦ Child sex ratio (0–6 years) – 919 females per 1000 males.

◦ Decadal growth rate (2001–2011) – 17.7%.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1084) among states and Haryana the lowest (879); among UTs, Puducherry was highest (1037) and Daman & Diu lowest (618).

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• The first Census in India was conducted in 1872 under Lord Mayo, and the first complete and synchronous Census in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

• The Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

question: Which bill passed in the Lok Sabha in 2022 seeks to convert the National Rail and Transportation Institute, Vadodara (a deemed university) to the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Central Universities (Amendment) Bill.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed by the Lok Sabha in 2022 to convert the National Rail and Transportation Institute (NRTI), Vadodara — a deemed-to-be university — into a central university named Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya.

• The Bill amended the Central Universities Act, 2009.

• The new university is meant to develop skilled manpower and research for the entire transport and mobility sector — railways, roads, ports, shipping, aviation and logistics — supporting the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.

• The Union Minister of Railways serves as the Chancellor of Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya (Visitor role for such institutions rests with the Government).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• An Appropriation Bill authorises the government to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund of India; it is a Money Bill under Article 110.

• The Competition (Amendment) Bill amends the Competition Act, 2002, which governs the Competition Commission of India (CCI).

• PM Gati Shakti was launched on 13 October 2021 as a national master plan for multimodal connectivity.

NOTE

• A Bill becomes an Act after being passed by both Houses and receiving the assent of the President (Article 111).

• NRTI Vadodara, set up in 2018, was India's first university dedicated to transportation.

question: Steapsin, the enzyme which converts fats into fatty acids and glycerol, is secreted by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is pancreas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Steapsin is another name for pancreatic lipase, and it is secreted by the pancreas as a part of pancreatic juice.

• It acts in the small intestine (duodenum) and breaks down emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

• The pancreas is a heterocrine (mixed) gland — it works both as an exocrine gland (pancreatic juice) and an endocrine gland (hormones insulin and glucagon from the Islets of Langerhans).

• Pancreatic juice contains three main enzymes:

◦ Trypsin – acts on proteins (converts proteins/peptones into peptides and amino acids).

◦ Amylopsin (pancreatic amylase) – acts on starch, converting it into maltose.

◦ Steapsin (pancreatic lipase) – acts on fats.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bile, produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder, contains no enzyme; it only emulsifies fat so that lipase can act on it.

• The stomach secretes gastric juice containing pepsin, rennin and hydrochloric acid.

• The small intestine secretes intestinal juice (succus entericus) containing enzymes such as maltase, sucrase, lactase, erepsin and intestinal lipase.

NOTE

• The largest gland in the human body is the liver; the pancreas is the second largest.

• Final absorption of digested food occurs mainly in the small intestine through finger-like projections called villi; the large intestine mainly absorbs water and salts.

question: English East India Company acquired Diwani of Bengal in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1765.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The English East India Company acquired the Diwani (the right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha in 1765.

• It was granted by the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II through the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), signed after the Battle of Buxar (1764).

• This marked the beginning of the Dual Government (Dyarchy) in Bengal, introduced by Robert Clive:

◦ The Company held the Diwani — revenue collection.

◦ The Nawab held the Nizamat — police and judicial administration.

◦ The system was abolished by Warren Hastings in 1772, when the Company took direct charge.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Battle of Plassey (1757) — Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah; it laid the foundation of British political power in India.

• Battle of Buxar (1764) — the British under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first British Parliamentary step to control the Company's Indian affairs; Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal.

NOTE

• The Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.

• The dual system caused severe misgovernment and contributed to the Great Bengal Famine of 1770.

question: President Draupadi Murmu launched the 'Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan' and the Nikshay 2.0 portal to eliminate Tuberculosis by ______ through a virtual event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2025.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• President Droupadi Murmu launched the "Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan" and the Ni-kshay 2.0 portal on 9 September 2022 through a virtual event.

• The goal of the campaign is to make India TB-free by 2025, which is five years ahead of the global Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of 2030.

• The campaign introduced the concept of "Ni-kshay Mitra" — individuals, organisations, corporates or elected representatives who adopt TB patients and provide nutritional, diagnostic and vocational support.

• Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, discovered by Robert Koch in 1882; it mainly affects the lungs and spreads through air (droplet infection).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana provides ₹500 per month (later revised) as nutritional support to every notified TB patient through Direct Benefit Transfer.

• World TB Day is observed on 24 March every year.

• The BCG (Bacillus Calmette–Guérin) vaccine protects against tuberculosis.

NOTE

• The programme is implemented by the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP), earlier called the Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP), under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

• Droupadi Murmu became the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022 and is the first tribal woman to hold the office.

question: Which among the following Buddhist Universities is located in Bihar, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nalanda University.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nalanda was the most famous ancient Buddhist Mahavihara (monastic university), located in present-day Nalanda district of Bihar, near Rajgir.

• It was founded in the 5th century CE by Kumaragupta I of the Gupta dynasty and flourished under later rulers, including Harshavardhana and the Palas.

• Chinese travellers Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) and I-tsing studied and taught here; Hiuen Tsang visited during the reign of Harshavardhana.

• It was destroyed around 1193 CE by Bakhtiyar Khalji. The ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Vallabhi University was located in Gujarat (Saurashtra) and was a great centre of Hinayana Buddhism.

• Somapura Mahavihara was built by Dharmapala of the Pala dynasty at Paharpur in present-day Bangladesh — also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Nabadwip in West Bengal was a centre of learning associated with Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and the Navya-Nyaya school, not a Buddhist university.

NOTE

• Other ancient centres of learning: Takshashila (Taxila) in present-day Pakistan, Vikramshila (Bihar, founded by Dharmapala), Odantapuri (Bihar) and Jagaddala (Bengal).

• A modern Nalanda University was re-established at Rajgir, Bihar, under the Nalanda University Act, 2010.

question: Who has been the chairman of Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) since 5 April, 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Manoj Soni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Manoj Soni took charge as the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on 5 April 2022.

• Before this he served as a Member of UPSC (joined in 2017) and had been Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University and of Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.

• Dr. T.C.A. Anant, Shri Bharat Bhushan Vyas and Ms. Smita Nagaraj were serving as Members of the Commission during that period.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The UPSC is a constitutional body established under Article 315 of the Constitution; Articles 315–323 (Part XIV) deal with Public Service Commissions.

• It consists of a Chairman and other members appointed by the President; they hold office for 6 years or till the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier (for a State PSC, the age limit is 62 years).

• Article 320 lays down the functions of the UPSC, and Article 322 provides that its expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

• The UPSC headquarters is at Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi.

NOTE

• The UPSC's origin lies in the Government of India Act, 1919, with the first Public Service Commission set up on 1 October 1926; its first Chairman was Sir Ross Barker.

• It became the Federal Public Service Commission under the Government of India Act, 1935, and was renamed Union Public Service Commission after Independence.

question: When was the first battle of Tarain fought?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1191.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191 between Prithviraj Chauhan (Prithviraj III) and Muhammad Ghori (Shihabuddin Muhammad Ghori).

• In this battle Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori, who was wounded and fled the field.

• Tarain (Taraori) is located near Thanesar in present-day Haryana.

• In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Muhammad Ghori returned with a larger force and defeated Prithviraj Chauhan — a turning point that laid the foundation of Muslim rule in northern India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• After Ghori's death in 1206, his slave general Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty, the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

• Prithviraj Chauhan's court poet Chand Bardai wrote the epic Prithviraj Raso.

• The Battle of Chandawar (1194) saw Muhammad Ghori defeat Jaichand of Kannauj.

NOTE

• Sequence to remember: First Battle of Tarain (1191) – Prithviraj wins; Second Battle of Tarain (1192) – Ghori wins; Battle of Chandawar (1194) – Ghori defeats Jaichand.

• The First Battle of Panipat (1526) later established the Mughal Empire under Babur.

question: Raja Parba festival of Odisha is the living cultural heritage and agricultural way of life. It is held for three days in the month of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is June.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raja Parba (also spelt Rajo) is a famous three-day festival of Odisha, celebrated in the month of June, at the onset of the monsoon.

• It celebrates womanhood and the menstruation of Mother Earth (Bhudevi), and it marks the beginning of the agricultural year.

• The three days are called Pahili Raja, Mithuna Sankranti (Raja Sankranti) and Bhu Daaha (Basi Raja); the fourth day is Vasumati Snana, the ceremonial bath of Bhudevi.

• During the festival women take rest from work, wear new clothes, play on decorated swings (doli) and eat the traditional cake Poda Pitha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other important festivals of Odisha: Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath at Puri, Nuakhai (harvest festival of western Odisha), Bali Jatra (Cuttack), Dhanu Jatra (Bargarh) and Konark Dance Festival.

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha; Chhau is a famous masked dance of the region.

NOTE

• Odisha's capital is Bhubaneswar, known as the "Temple City of India"; the Sun Temple at Konark and the Jagannath Temple at Puri are its most famous monuments.

• Chilika Lake in Odisha is Asia's largest brackish water lagoon and a Ramsar site.

question: According to census 2011, which state has highest decadal population growth rate between 2001 – 11?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Census 2011, Meghalaya recorded the highest decadal population growth rate among the States during 2001–2011, at about 27.9%.

• The lowest decadal growth rate among States was in Nagaland (–0.6%), which actually showed a decline in population.

• India's overall decadal growth rate for 2001–2011 was 17.7%, the sharpest decline in growth rate since Independence.

• Bihar (25.4%) was the second highest among the States, followed by Jammu & Kashmir and Arunachal Pradesh (26.0%).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala recorded one of the lowest growth rates (4.9%) among the major states.

• Among the Union Territories, Dadra & Nagar Haveli recorded a very high growth rate (over 55%).

• Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state and Sikkim the least populous state; Bihar has the highest population density (1106 persons/sq km) and Arunachal Pradesh the lowest (17).

NOTE

• The year 1921 is called the "Great Divide" or Year of the Great Divide in Indian demography, because it was the last year in which India's population declined.

• The year 1951 is called the "Year of the Small Divide".

question: Who gave the slogan, "Freedom is my birth right and I shall have it!"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous slogan "Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it" was given by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

• He was called "Lokmanya" and was described by the British as "the Father of Indian Unrest".

• He was one of the trio of extremist leaders known as "Lal–Bal–Pal" — Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.

• He started the newspapers "Kesari" (Marathi) and "Maratha" (English), and popularised Ganapati Utsav and Shivaji Utsav to build national feeling.

• Along with Annie Besant, he launched the Home Rule Movement in 1916.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Badruddin Tyabji was the third President of the Indian National Congress (Madras session, 1887) and its first Muslim President.

• Lala Lajpat Rai, called "Punjab Kesari", died after a lathi charge during the Simon Commission protest (1928) at Lahore.

• Bipin Chandra Pal is known as the "Father of Revolutionary Thoughts in India".

NOTE

• Tilak wrote Gita Rahasya and The Arctic Home in the Vedas while in prison at Mandalay (Burma).

• Other famous slogans: "Do or Die" – Mahatma Gandhi; "Inquilab Zindabad" – Bhagat Singh (popularised); "Jai Hind" and "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom" – Subhas Chandra Bose; "Jai Jawan Jai Kisan" – Lal Bahadur Shastri.

question: ______ is scheduled to host the International Cricket Council (ICC) Men's Cricket World Cup 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 was scheduled to be hosted by India, and it was the 13th edition of the tournament.

• This was the first time India hosted the Cricket World Cup alone; earlier editions in the subcontinent were co-hosted (1987 and 1996 with Pakistan/Sri Lanka, and 2011 with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh).

• The final was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, the largest cricket stadium in the world by seating capacity.

• India has won the ODI World Cup twice — in 1983 (captain Kapil Dev) and 2011 (captain M.S. Dhoni).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975, won by West Indies.

• Australia is the most successful team in the history of the ODI World Cup.

• The ICC (International Cricket Council) was founded in 1909 as the Imperial Cricket Conference; its headquarters is in Dubai, UAE.

NOTE

• India won the first T20 World Cup in 2007 under M.S. Dhoni.

• The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) was established in 1928 and is headquartered in Mumbai.

question: Who among the following is famous for playing the musical instrument 'Sarod'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amjad Ali Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a world-renowned Indian classical musician famous for playing the Sarod, a stringed instrument of Hindustani classical music.

• He belongs to the Senia Bangash gharana and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan (2001).

• Other famous Sarod players: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan (father of Amjad Ali Khan) and Buddhadev Dasgupta.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ustad Bismillah Khan – Shehnai (a wind instrument); he was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

• Ustad Zakir Hussain – Tabla (a percussion instrument); son of Ustad Alla Rakha.

• Pandit Ravi Shankar – Sitar; he received the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian musical instruments: Tata Vadya (string – sitar, sarod, veena, violin), Sushira Vadya (wind – flute, shehnai, nadaswaram), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane – tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj) and Ghana Vadya (solid percussion – manjira, jaltarang).

• Other artist–instrument pairs: Hariprasad Chaurasia – Flute; Shivkumar Sharma – Santoor; Vilayat Khan – Sitar; N. Rajam – Violin.

question:
Identify the famous Indian classical dancer.

She is a Guru of both Bharatanatyam and Odissi dancing style. She received Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1987.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sonal Mansingh is an eminent Indian classical dancer and Guru of both Bharatanatyam and Odissi.

• She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1987, the Padma Bhushan (1992) and the Padma Vibhushan (2003).

• She was nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the President of India in 2018.

• She founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD) in New Delhi in 1977.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Shovana Narayan is a celebrated Kathak dancer and a former Indian Audit and Accounts Service officer.

• Padma Subrahmanyam is a renowned Bharatanatyam dancer and researcher, known for reviving Karanas of the Natya Shastra.

• Mrinalini Sarabhai was a famous Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer and founder of the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, Ahmedabad.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, was set up in 1953.

question: In 1867, Keshab Chandra Sen helped Atmaram Pandurang found the Prarthana Samaj in ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 in Bombay (present-day Mumbai) by Atmaram Pandurang, with the encouragement and help of Keshab Chandra Sen of the Brahmo Samaj.

• It was a socio-religious reform movement in Western India that worked for:

◦ Opposition to the caste system and untouchability.

◦ Widow remarriage and women's education.

◦ Raising the age of marriage for boys and girls.

• Its most prominent leaders were Mahadev Govind Ranade, R. G. Bhandarkar and N. G. Chandavarkar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Brahmo Samaj was founded in Calcutta in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy; Keshab Chandra Sen later led one of its branches.

• The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 at Bombay by Swami Dayanand Saraswati, who gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas".

• The Ramakrishna Mission was founded in 1897 by Swami Vivekananda.

NOTE

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance"; the abolition of Sati in 1829 by Lord William Bentinck was largely due to his efforts.

• Mahadev Govind Ranade also founded the Widow Marriage Association and was a founder of the Indian National Social Conference.

question: The famous Hirakud Captive Thermal Power plant is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hirakud Captive Thermal Power Plant is located in the Sambalpur district of Odisha, near the Hirakud region.

• It is a captive power plant — that is, a power plant set up by an industry (here Hindalco Industries) mainly to supply electricity to its own factory (the aluminium smelter) rather than to the public grid.

• The Hirakud Dam, built on the Mahanadi river in Odisha, is one of the longest earthen dams in the world; it was inaugurated in 1957 by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other important thermal power stations of Odisha: Talcher Super Thermal Power Station (NTPC), Ib Valley and Darlipali.

• Odisha is rich in minerals — iron ore, bauxite, chromite, manganese and coal — which is why aluminium and steel industries are concentrated there.

NOTE

• Thermal power contributes the largest share of India's installed electricity generation capacity, mainly through coal.

• Multipurpose river valley projects: Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej), Damodar Valley (Damodar), Nagarjuna Sagar (Krishna), Tehri (Bhagirathi) and Hirakud (Mahanadi).

question: As a result of which act did Queen Victoria, who was the monarch of Britain, also became the sovereign of British territories in India, with the title "Empress of India" in 1858?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government Of India Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of India Act, 1858 was passed after the Revolt of 1857, and it transferred the government of India from the East India Company to the British Crown — that is, to Queen Victoria.

• Key provisions of the Act of 1858 (also called the Act for the Good Government of India):

◦ It abolished the East India Company and the system of Double Government (Board of Control and Court of Directors).

◦ It created the office of the Secretary of State for India, a member of the British Cabinet, assisted by a 15-member Council of India.

◦ The Governor-General of India was given the additional title of Viceroy, the representative of the Crown; Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.

• Queen Victoria's Proclamation was read out by Lord Canning at Allahabad on 1 November 1858.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Regulating Act, 1773 was the first step by the British Parliament to control the Company; it made Warren Hastings the Governor-General of Bengal.

• The Charter Acts of 1793, 1813, 1833 and 1853 renewed the Company's charter; the Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly (except tea and trade with China), and the Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck being the first).

• The Indian Councils Acts of 1861, 1892 and 1909 dealt with the expansion of the legislative councils; the Act of 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

NOTE

• The formal assumption of the title "Kaiser-i-Hind (Empress of India)" by Queen Victoria took place under the Royal Titles Act, 1876, and was proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar of 1877 during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton — the sovereignty over India, however, passed to the Crown in 1858 by this Act.

• The Government of India Act, 1935 was the longest Act passed by the British Parliament and became the main source of the Constitution of India.

question: When was the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana launched by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) was launched on 1 May 2016 from Ballia, Uttar Pradesh, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

• Objective: to provide free LPG (deposit-free) connections to women of Below Poverty Line (BPL) households, so as to:

◦ Reduce the health hazards caused by smoke from traditional cooking fuels such as wood, coal and cow dung.

◦ Prevent indoor air pollution and deforestation.

◦ Empower women and give them a smoke-free kitchen.

• The slogan of the scheme is "Swachh Indhan, Behtar Jeevan".

• Ujjwala 2.0 was launched in August 2021 from Mahoba, Uttar Pradesh, with additional connections and a free first refill plus stove.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other schemes launched in 2016: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, Startup India, Stand-Up India and Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana.

• PAHAL (DBTL) is the scheme that transfers LPG subsidy directly into bank accounts.

NOTE

• LPG (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) consists mainly of butane and propane; ethyl mercaptan is added to give it a smell so that leakage can be detected.

• Related welfare schemes: Saubhagya (electricity connections, 2017), Swachh Bharat Mission (2014), Jan Dhan Yojana (2014) and Ayushman Bharat (2018).

question: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme was launched by which ministry?
option_4: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme was launched on 1 June 2020 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).

• It is a micro-credit scheme launched to help street vendors whose livelihood was badly affected by the COVID-19 lockdown.

• Main features:

◦ A collateral-free working capital loan of up to ₹10,000 for one year in the first tranche, with enhanced loans of ₹20,000 and ₹50,000 on timely repayment.

◦ An interest subsidy of 7% per annum on regular repayment, credited quarterly to the beneficiary's account.

◦ Cashback incentives on digital transactions to promote a digital economy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other schemes of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban), AMRUT, Smart Cities Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) and Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – NULM.

• Street vendors are legally protected by the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014.

NOTE

• "AtmaNirbhar Bharat Abhiyan" was announced in May 2020 as a special economic package to make India self-reliant.

• Remember scheme–ministry pairs, a favourite SSC question type: PM-KISAN – Ministry of Agriculture; MGNREGA – Ministry of Rural Development; Ujjwala – Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; Ayushman Bharat – Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

question: ______ species are those species of plants and animals which are found exclusively in a particular area.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Endemic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Endemic species are those species of plants and animals that are found exclusively in a particular geographical area and nowhere else in the world. (स्थानिक प्रजातियाँ)

◦ Examples in India: the Asiatic Lion (Gir, Gujarat), the Nilgiri Tahr (Western Ghats), the Lion-tailed Macaque (Western Ghats) and the Sangai deer (Keibul Lamjao, Manipur).

◦ Endemism is high in isolated regions such as islands and mountain ranges — the Western Ghats and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands are Indian biodiversity hotspots rich in endemic species.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Endangered species – species whose numbers have fallen so low that they are in danger of extinction if the causal factors continue to operate.

• Critically Endangered species – species facing an extremely high risk of extinction in the immediate future (e.g., the Great Indian Bustard).

• Threatened species – an umbrella category of the IUCN that includes Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered species.

• Other IUCN categories: Extinct, Extinct in the Wild, Near Threatened, Least Concern and Data Deficient.

NOTE

• The IUCN Red List, maintained by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (founded 1948, headquarters at Gland, Switzerland), records the conservation status of species.

• India has four biodiversity hotspots: the Himalaya, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, the Indo-Burma region and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

question: Which among the following is a subject of State List in Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Agriculture is a subject of the State List (List II) of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, so State Legislatures can make laws on it.

• The Seventh Schedule (Article 246) divides legislative powers into three lists:

◦ Union List (List I) – originally 97 subjects (now 100): defence, foreign affairs, railways, banking, currency, atomic energy, posts and telegraphs.

◦ State List (List II) – originally 66 subjects (now 61): public order, police, agriculture, public health and sanitation, local government, land.

◦ Concurrent List (List III) – originally 47 subjects (now 52): education, forests, criminal law and procedure, marriage and divorce, weights and measures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Banking and Railways are subjects of the Union List.

• Regarding Ports: major ports fall under the Union List, while ports other than major ports are in the State List — since the option simply says "Ports", the intended answer of the paper is Agriculture, which is unambiguously a State subject.

• In case of a conflict between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent subject, the Union law prevails (Article 254).

NOTE

• Residuary powers (subjects not mentioned in any list) rest with the Union Parliament under Article 248 — a feature borrowed from Canada.

• Education, forests, weights and measures, and protection of wild animals and birds were shifted from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

question: Pung Cholom is performed usually on religious occasions to the accompaniment of songs and dhol. It is famously performed in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pung Cholom (also called Mridanga Kirtan or Dhumal) is a classical drum dance of Manipur, performed by male dancers who play the pung (a Manipuri drum) while dancing.

• It is usually performed on religious and festive occasions, especially as a prelude to Manipuri Raas Leela and Sankirtana performances.

• The dance is known for its acrobatic movements, leaps and spins, combined with soft, graceful body control.

• Manipuri Sankirtana — ritual singing, drumming and dancing of Manipur — was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manipuri is one of the eight classical dance forms of India; its most famous form is the Raas Leela, based on the theme of Radha and Krishna.

• Other dances of Manipur: Thang-Ta (a martial art dance), Lai Haraoba and Dhol Cholom.

• Famous festivals of Manipur: Yaoshang, Ningol Chakouba and the Sangai Festival.

NOTE

• Folk dances by state: Bihu (Assam), Garba/Dandiya (Gujarat), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Lavani (Maharashtra), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand/West Bengal), Kalbelia (Rajasthan) and Theyyam (Kerala).

• The capital of Manipur is Imphal; Loktak Lake, the largest freshwater lake in North-East India, is famous for its floating phumdis and Keibul Lamjao National Park.

question: Major plantations are found in the ______ region of the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Plantation agriculture is mainly practised in the tropical and sub-tropical regions of the world, because these areas have high temperature, heavy rainfall and a long growing season — conditions ideal for crops such as tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane, banana, cocoa and spices.

• Features of plantation agriculture:

◦ It is a single-crop (monoculture), large-scale, commercial type of farming.

◦ It requires large capital investment, scientific management and abundant cheap labour.

◦ The produce is mainly meant for export/industrial processing, so good transport links between the estate and the market are essential.

• Examples: tea in Assam and West Bengal, coffee in Karnataka and Kerala, rubber in Kerala, banana and sugarcane in tropical belts, and cocoa in West Africa.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Plantation agriculture was introduced in India and other colonies by the Europeans (British) during the colonial period.

• Grassland regions (Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, Downs, Velds) are chiefly used for extensive commercial grain farming and livestock rearing, not plantations.

• Temperate regions practise mixed farming, dairy farming and market gardening; desert regions support only oasis or irrigated farming and nomadic herding.

NOTE

• Other major types of farming: shifting cultivation (jhum), subsistence farming, intensive farming, extensive farming, dairy farming, horticulture and sericulture (silk).

• India is the largest producer of tea in the world after China, and Assam is India's largest tea-producing state.
